otp_check.question: NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_SHOW_OTP is turned on in .env, and .env also sets NODE_ENV to a non-production value. Can a password-reset code reach a browser in a production build?
otp_check.answer: No. Checked on the real build, built with this .env.
otp_check.compiled_code: In .next-qa/server/app/api/auth/forgot-password/request-otp/route.js the helper devOtpForResponse is `function f(e){}`. Next replaced process.env.NODE_ENV with production at build time and removed the rest, so the NODE_ENV line in .env cannot bring it back.
otp_check.real_run: runtime-prod.json, port 3977. POST /api/auth/forgot-password/request-otp for a real test account: 200, keys [message], no devOtp, no 6 digits in the body. A second request got cooldownRemaining, which proves the first really made a code. POST /api/profile/mobile-otp/request, signed in: the same. GET /forgot-password: no [Dev mode] text.
otp_check.leftover: The page's render branch for `[Dev mode] OTP:` is still in the chunks for /forgot-password and /profile. It only shows if the API sends devOtp, which this build cannot do.
otp_check.dev_server: With `next dev` and this .env, the code IS returned: that is the documented behaviour (README section Dev-mode OTPs) and the unit test covers the branch. See SCAN-4. A real dev server run was not done: the shared machine had about 2.5 GB free.
